title: Citation Graphs Over Time

The focus is on directed edges from a citing work to a cited work, each edge carrying a publication date or timestamp. crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Citation graphs over time map how scholarly works reference one another and how those references accumulate, shift, or fade across years. The focus is on directed edges from a citing work to a cited work, each edge carrying a publication date or timestamp. This view supports discovery of foundational papers, rising clusters, and research fronts within a field. It is used by researchers and librarians to trace intellectual lineage rather than to rank individual authors.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on bibliographic records and full-text reference lists stored in a graph database or a linked-data index. Each node is a paper, book, or dataset, and each edge is a citation with a year or date. Temporal queries are handled by indexing edges by time, often with incremental updates as new works are added. The site's own library of 135 research papers and 91 AI books can serve as a small seed corpus for such a graph, but the method scales to external open citation indexes.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by parsing reference sections and metadata to extract cited works, then matching those works to unique identifiers such as DOIs or titles. A directed graph is built with nodes for works and edges for citations, each edge stamped with the citing work's publication date. Analysts then compute time series of citation counts, co-citation clusters, and paths of influence, often using network measures like betweenness or burst detection. The result is a temporal map that shows not just who cites whom, but when and in what sequence.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on provenance and completeness. Citation data comes from published reference lists, so the original paper remains the authoritative source, and the site links to that original paper rather than to any third-party search tool. Risks include missing citations, ambiguous author names, and retracted works that continue to be cited. A responsible graph keeps a record of extraction date and source for each edge, and flags retractions or corrections where known.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Citation graphs over time are moving toward live updating and predictive views of research influence. Future work may combine temporal citation edges with extracted claims, such as the 11,222 claims currently held in the site's library, to show how specific findings propagate or are contradicted. The direction is toward interactive timelines, field-level maps of emerging topics, and better handling of preprint and versioned works.
